You have a duty to protect Salt Lake City from violence, civil unrest and destruction and devaluation of property. If you collect tax revenue for stated purposes and then fail to support the objectives of those sources, you are in breach of duty and you subject the city to civil liability. Apologizing to the Carbajal family when you did was irresponsible, and was disloyal to your police department. While all of our hearts go out to the Carbajal family, those of us who are familiar with precedent case law in this specific area expected Sim Gill's conclusion, which was legally correct in every way. Apologizing for the correct actions of the police officers involved weakened your integrity as one that should put support of a good law enforcement agency as a top priority. You either had or should have had reasonable advance knowledge of the recent protests that affected Salt Lake City, particularly the first one where a police car was destroyed and other property was damaged. What did you do to protect your city, your citizens and your police department? All reports point to your tying the hands of the police department and facilitating a liberal agenda, which would include inciting unrest, similar to the actions of other Democrat politicians around the nation, in an effort to affect November elections in a rather counterfeit fashion. On July 18th, protesters were allowed to gather in front of the governor's mansion, they illegally used their own cars to block traffic. City streets and access to businesses were shut down, allowing protesters to march from the governor's mansion to the State Capitol. Last week, you allowed protesters to unlawfully assemble, block traffic and cause hundreds of thousands of dollars of damage to the new D.A.'s office. Hear this loud and clear: Utah residents were and are disgusted with your lack of courage and leadership and for your inaction in allowing these things to happen and we will not stand for it. Salt Lake City is not Seattle. It is not Los Angeles. We are better than that, and need to behave better than what we have seen from other cities, where the leadership is determined to destroy whom and what they have stewardship over, in an effort to push a political agenda. You have been granted a sacred duty to serve and protect the citizens, not a political party, an agenda, or a personal vision. Your legacy as a mayor is for you to shape. You can be remembered and revered as an effective leader of a great community, or you can be remembered as a disgrace, where years of disaster cleanup followed your administration. Please put the great people of Salt Lake City and the surrounding communities first. Politics are insignificant compared to the personal and financial security of our residents. Please show the people of our community that your priorities are in the right place. Truly responsible leadership, that which is driven by a love for the people and not loyalty to a cause, is always rewarded at re-election time. If you wish to continue to serve, please help our community by doing the right things as mayor.

My name is Nicole Giambastiani and I am concerned for the wellbeing of ALL people in this country. I am writing to demand that the City Council adopt a budget for the people, that prioritizes community wellbeing and redirects funding away from the police. We are in the midst of widespread upheaval over the systemic violence of policing, embodied by the SLCPD?s well documented history of lethal force against residents of color. Empty gestures and suggestions of reform are unacceptable. I am demanding the voices of this movement be heard, and that real change be made to the way this city allocates its resources. Support for marginalized communities is necessary now, more than ever. But instead, the Mayor has proposed an increase in funding to the SLCPD, while social services and education--proven to better promote community safety than policing--stagnate. The SLCPD has seen a rise in overtime pay which, when too often paid out to officers responsible for harassing unhoused, Black, Indigenous, and Latinx residents, is deeply insulting. I am demanding that the City Council defund the SLCPD. I demand a budget that adequately and effectively meets the needs of impacted Utahns during this trying and uncertain time, when livelihoods are on the line. I demand a budget that supports community wellbeing, rather than empowering the police forces that tear us apart. Although City Council has thus far avoided voting or revising Mayor Mendenhall?s budget proposal, the document is back in your hands. It is your duty to represent your constituents. I am urging you to completely revise the SLC budget for 2020-2021 fiscal year, and to fund care, not criminalization and incarceration. You must adopt a budget for the people. Public opinion is with me. Thank you for your time, Nicole Giambastiani
